A Storage resource tells the Director how to reach a Storage Daemon and which of its devices and media type to use.

## Examples

**Disk storage**

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Address = backup.example.com
  Password = "storage-secret"
  Device = FileStorage
  Media Type = File
  Maximum Concurrent Jobs = 10
}
```

### Name {#d-name}

Key: `name` · Type: name · Required

Name of the Storage resource as jobs and pools refer to it.

```text
Storage {
  Name = "File"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File
```

### Description {#d-description}

Key: `description` · Type: string

Free text describing the storage.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Description = "Disk storage in the server room"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File description="Disk storage in the server room"
```

### Protocol {#d-protocol}

Key: `protocol` · Type: enum · Default: `Native` · Values: `Native`, `NDMPv2`, `NDMPv3`, `NDMPv4`

Protocol to the storage: Native, or NDMP for NDMP tape servers.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Protocol = Native
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File protocol=Native
```

Key: `authtype` · Type: enum · Default: `None` · Values: `None`, `Clear`, `MD5`

Authentication for NDMP storage: None, Clear or MD5.

Storage {
  Name = File
  Auth Type = None

### Address {#d-address}

Key: `address` · Type: string · Aliases: SD Address · Required

Host name or IP address of the Storage Daemon, as the File Daemons must reach it: the Director passes it on to the client. Do not use localhost when clients run on other hosts.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Address = "backup.example.com"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File address=backup.example.com
```

### Lan Address {#d-lanaddress}

Key: `lanaddress` · Type: string

Address used instead of Address for clients in passive mode on a separate LAN.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Lan Address = "10.0.0.5"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File lanaddress=10.0.0.5
```

### Port {#d-port}

Key: `port` · Type: positive integer · Default: `9103` · Aliases: SD Port

TCP port of the Storage Daemon.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Port = 9103
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File port=9103
```

Key: `username` · Type: string

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Username = "ndmp"

```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File username=ndmp
```

### Password {#d-password}

Key: `password` · Type: password · Aliases: SD Password · Required

Password shared with the Storage Daemon's Director resource (and TLS-PSK key).

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Password = "storage-secret"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com device=FileStorage mediatype=File password=storage-secret
```

### Device {#d-device}

Key: `device` · Type: string list · Required

Name of a Device (or Autochanger) resource in the Storage Daemon. It must match the name there exactly. Several devices may be listed.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Device = "FileStorage"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret mediatype=File device=FileStorage
```

### Media Type {#d-mediatype}

Key: `mediatype` · Type: string · Required

Media type of the volumes this storage writes. The Director only uses volumes of this media type with it, so different kinds of media (or different directories of file storage) need different media types. It must match Media Type of the device in the Storage Daemon.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Media Type = "File"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File
```

### Auto Changer {#d-autochanger}

Key: `autochanger` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

The device is an autochanger (tape library); slots and barcodes are used for label, update slots and mount.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Auto Changer = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File autochanger=yes
```

### Enabled {#d-enabled}

Key: `enabled` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

A disabled storage is not used for new jobs; enable/disable storage change it at run time.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Enabled = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File enabled=yes
```

### Allow Compression {#d-allowcompression}

Key: `allowcompression` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Allow software compression by the File Daemon for jobs writing here. Set it to no for tape drives that compress in hardware.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Allow Compression = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File allowcompression=yes
```

### Heartbeat Interval {#d-heartbeatinterval}

Key: `heartbeatinterval` · Type: time · Default: `0`

Interval of keep-alive packets to the Storage Daemon. 0 switches it off. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Heartbeat Interval = 60
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File heartbeatinterval=60
```

### Cache Status Interval {#d-cachestatusinterval}

Key: `cachestatusinterval` · Type: time · Default: `30`

How long the Director caches the status of the Storage Daemon. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Cache Status Interval = 30
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File cachestatusinterval=30
```

### Maximum Concurrent Jobs {#d-maximumconcurrentjobs}

Key: `maximumconcurrentjobs` · Type: positive integer · Default: `1`

How many jobs may use this storage at the same time. With disk storage and several devices it can be raised; the device's own Maximum Concurrent Jobs in the Storage Daemon limits as well (the Director cannot read that one).

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Maximum Concurrent Jobs = 10
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File maximumconcurrentjobs=10
```

### Maximum Concurrent Read Jobs {#d-maximumconcurrentreadjobs}

Key: `maximumconcurrentreadjobs` · Type: positive integer · Default: `0`

How many of the concurrent jobs may read (restore, copy, migrate source); 0 means no own limit.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Maximum Concurrent Read Jobs = 2
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File maximumconcurrentreadjobs=2
```

### Paired Storage {#d-pairedstorage}

Key: `pairedstorage` · Type: resource

For NDMP: the native storage that holds the data of an NDMP backup that Bareos stores itself.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Paired Storage = "File"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File pairedstorage=File
```

### Maximum Bandwidth Per Job {#d-maximumbandwidthperjob}

Key: `maximumbandwidthperjob` · Type: speed

Limits the bandwidth of each job on this storage. Speeds take the suffixes k/s, m/s (powers of 1024) or kb/s, mb/s (powers of 1000); a plain number means bytes per second.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Maximum Bandwidth Per Job = 50 m/s
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File maximumbandwidthperjob="50 m/s"
```

### Collect Statistics {#d-collectstatistics}

Key: `collectstatistics` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no` · Deprecated

Deprecated: collect device statistics in the catalog.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  Collect Statistics = no
}
```

### NDMP Changer Device {#d-ndmpchangerdevice}

Key: `ndmpchangerdevice` · Type: string

Changer device of an NDMP tape server.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  NDMP Changer Device = "/dev/sg0"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File ndmpchangerdevice=/dev/sg0
```

### TLS Authenticate {#d-tlsauthenticate}

Key: `tlsauthenticate` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Use TLS only to authenticate the peer and switch back to an unencrypted connection afterwards. The data then travels in clear text, so this is meant for networks that are protected otherwise. Bareos' default TLS-PSK setup does not need it.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Authenticate = no
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsauthenticate=no
```

### TLS Enable {#d-tlsenable}

Key: `tlsenable` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Enable TLS for this connection. Since Bareos 18.2 TLS is on by default and uses TLS-PSK with the password of the resource, so no certificates are needed; set it to no only for peers that cannot speak TLS.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Enable = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsenable=yes
```

### TLS Require {#d-tlsrequire}

Key: `tlsrequire` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Refuse connections that do not use TLS. With the default (yes) a peer without TLS cannot connect; set it to no only during a migration from very old clients.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Require = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsrequire=yes
```

### TLS Cipher List {#d-tlscipherlist}

Key: `tlscipherlist` · Type: string

OpenSSL cipher list for TLS 1.2 and older, colon separated. Leave it empty to use the OpenSSL defaults; restrict it only when a security policy demands specific ciphers.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Cipher List = "PSK-AES256-GCM-SHA384:PSK-AES128-GCM-SHA256"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlscipherlist=PSK-AES256-GCM-SHA384:PSK-AES128-GCM-SHA256
```

### TLS Cipher Suites {#d-tlsciphersuites}

Key: `tlsciphersuites` · Type: string

OpenSSL cipher suites for TLS 1.3, colon separated. Empty means the OpenSSL defaults.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Cipher Suites = "TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsciphersuites=TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256
```

### TLS DH File {#d-tlsdhfile}

Key: `tlsdhfile` · Type: path

PEM file with Diffie-Hellman parameters for the DH key exchange of TLS 1.2. Without it, ephemeral DH ciphers are not offered; ECDHE and PSK ciphers do not need it.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS DH File = "/etc/bareos/tls/dh2048.pem"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsdhfile=/etc/bareos/tls/dh2048.pem
```

### TLS Protocol {#d-tlsprotocol}

Key: `tlsprotocol` · Type: string

Restricts the TLS protocol versions in OpenSSL syntax, for example to forbid old versions. Empty means the OpenSSL default.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Protocol = "-ALL, +TLSv1.2, +TLSv1.3"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsprotocol="-ALL, +TLSv1.2, +TLSv1.3"
```

### TLS Verify Peer {#d-tlsverifypeer}

Key: `tlsverifypeer` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

With certificate based TLS: check the peer's certificate against the CA and, for a server, against TLS Allowed CN. It has no effect with TLS-PSK.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Verify Peer = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsverifypeer=yes
```

### TLS Ca Certificate File {#d-tlscacertificatefile}

Key: `tlscacertificatefile` · Type: path

PEM file with the CA certificates used to verify the peer's certificate. Needed for certificate based TLS when TLS Verify Peer is on (or use TLS CA Certificate Dir).

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Ca Certificate File = "/etc/bareos/tls/ca.pem"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlscacertificatefile=/etc/bareos/tls/ca.pem
```

### TLS Ca Certificate Dir {#d-tlscacertificatedir}

Key: `tlscacertificatedir` · Type: path

Directory of hashed CA certificates (as made by openssl rehash), an alternative to TLS CA Certificate File.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Ca Certificate Dir = "/etc/ssl/certs"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlscacertificatedir=/etc/ssl/certs
```

### TLS Certificate Revocation List {#d-tlscertificaterevocationlist}

Key: `tlscertificaterevocationlist` · Type: path

PEM file with a certificate revocation list; certificates on it are refused.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Certificate Revocation List = "/etc/bareos/tls/crl.pem"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlscertificaterevocationlist=/etc/bareos/tls/crl.pem
```

### TLS Certificate {#d-tlscertificate}

Key: `tlscertificate` · Type: path

PEM file with the own certificate for certificate based TLS. Goes together with TLS Key.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Certificate = "/etc/bareos/tls/bareos-dir.pem"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlscertificate=/etc/bareos/tls/bareos-dir.pem
```

### TLS Key {#d-tlskey}

Key: `tlskey` · Type: path

PEM file with the private key of TLS Certificate. Keep it readable for the daemon user only.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Key = "/etc/bareos/tls/bareos-dir.key"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlskey=/etc/bareos/tls/bareos-dir.key
```

### TLS Allowed CN {#d-tlsallowedcn}

Key: `tlsallowedcn` · Type: string list

Common names a peer certificate may carry; others are refused when TLS Verify Peer is on. Repeat the directive for several names.

```text
Storage {
  Name = File
  TLS Allowed CN = "client1.example.com"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add storage name=File address=backup.example.com password=storage-secret device=FileStorage mediatype=File tlsallowedcn=client1.example.com
```
